title: Build a worker pool in Go — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a goroutine worker pool: turn 1 adds Submit()/Start(), turn 2 adds result collection, turn 3 adds Shutdown()/drain.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `Start()` in `pool/pool.go`: launch `p.workers` goroutines, each reading from `p.tasks`, calling `task.Fn()`, and sending a `Result{ID: task.ID, Value: result}` to `p.results`. Add each goroutine to `p.wg`. Run `go test ./...`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `Shutdown()`: close `p.tasks` to signal workers to stop, wait for all workers via `p.wg.Wait()`, then close `p.results` so callers can range over it. Use `p.once` to ensure Shutdown is idempotent. Run `go test ./...` and fix any failures.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time — all 4 tests must pass. Make sure TestAllResultsReceived can range over Results() to completion after Shutdown().
success_criteria: Workers read tasks, execute Fn, send results
Shutdown() signals workers and waits for completion
Results channel is closed after Shutdown so range terminates
